archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-rhythm)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old rhythm thrower who wins from a clean pocket on short and play-action timing throws, gives almost nothing with his legs, and lives or dies on whether the line holds long enough for his reads to come open.

report.headline: Cousins' rebound is real underneath, but the touchdown rate is running hot
report.take:
Cousins arrived in Las Vegas off the worst full-time season of his prime-era career. In 2025 he posted 0.024 EPA per play and a -2.8 CPOE, both ranked mid-40s or worse among qualifiers, and it looked like the end of the line. Five games into 2026 he is back near his Minnesota level: 0.191 EPA per dropback (14th), a positive CPOE and a 3-2 record with an offense whose run game ranks 29th in EPA. The rebound is mostly substance. He is a pocket passer and nothing else, with -2 rushing yards and three scrambles, so everything rides on the arm and the timing.

The engine is the short game. On 89 throws under 10 air yards he completes 73% for +0.27 EPA a play, with six touchdowns and no picks. Brock Bowers is the one target producing at a high level on volume (0.511 EPA per target on 34 looks). He also takes sacks at a low rate for how often he holds the ball: a 2.94-second time to throw, yet only 12.8% of pressures become sacks (5th). That matters behind a line that ranks 27th in hit rate allowed. The weak spots are just as clear. Throws behind the line are a drain (-0.414 EPA on 23 attempts), which matches Ashton Jeanty's flat 0.006-below-zero EPA per target. The 10-19 yard window has produced all four interceptions with a -7.2 CPOE.

The numbers flatter him in two places. Twelve touchdowns on 172 attempts is a 7% rate, and ten of them came on 28 red-zone attempts completed at only 53.6%. That is a conversion streak, not a repeatable skill at that level. The deep ball is the other: +0.874 EPA and a +12.9 CPOE on 20 attempts is a lovely month, but 20 throws is a hint. He has never been a vertical passer, with an intended air yardage of 8.4 and a career aDOT in the 7-8 range. Some of his raw output also comes from script. The 52-attempt, 365-yard Chiefs game and the blowout in New England, where he played 83% of snaps, both inflated volume.

Going forward, the efficiency should settle somewhere between his 2023 and 2024 form: a top-15 to top-20 passer by EPA rather than a top-10 one. The touchdown pace should drift toward the 1.5-to-2 per game range. The yardage floor is supported by a defense that can't run the ball and a defense of its own that leaks short completions, which keeps him throwing.

strengths.title: Efficient, turnover-free short passing
strengths.body: The quick game is where his accuracy and processing still show up: high completion rate, positive CPOE, six touchdowns and no interceptions inside 10 air yards. This has been his identity for a decade, so it is the most bankable part of the profile.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks despite holding it
strengths.body: He holds the ball nearly three seconds but converts few pressures into sacks, ranking 5th. That skill has shown up in his career lines before, with pressure-to-sack rates in the 17-21% range in his better years. It shields a line that allows hits at a bottom-six rate. Expect it to hold, though a 38-year-old's escape margin is thin if the pressure rate climbs.

strengths.title: Bowers as the reliable outlet
strengths.body: Bowers leads the team in targets and produces over half a point of EPA per look. That gives Cousins a middle-of-field answer on third down and in the red zone. Bowers' role is stable, so this should keep carrying the passing game.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate built on red-zone luck
concerns.body: Ten red-zone touchdowns on 28 attempts, while completing barely half of them, is an unsustainable mix. His overall TD rate ranks 7th, which is above anything his efficiency profile supports long term. Expect the touchdown total to slow even if the yardage holds.

concerns.title: Intermediate window is where turnovers live
concerns.body: All four interceptions have come on 10-19 yard throws, where his completion rate sinks below 50% with a -7.2 CPOE. Middle-of-field accuracy is also negative. This lines up with the 2025 decline and with his history of double-digit interception seasons. It is a real flaw that age is unlikely to fix.

concerns.title: No help from the run or screens
concerns.body: The offense ranks 29th in rush EPA. His throws behind the line lose value, and Jeanty's targets are break-even at best. That leaves Cousins to carry drives through the air with no rushing contribution of his own. The volume this creates is good for his counting stats, but it is a structural limit on the offense.

trend.note: After a 160-yard opener, his game-level passing EPA climbed and then held in the 6-10 range for four straight weeks. Fantasy output swung with touchdowns and script, peaking at 22.6 against Kansas City and falling to 13.7 in the New England blowout.

nextGame.headline: Indoor shootout against a bottom-three pass defense
nextGame.body:
Buffalo is the softest pass defense he has faced. It ranks 29th in pass EPA allowed and 30th in success rate, and it gives quarterbacks 314 yards and 2.6 touchdowns a game. It also ranks 27th against short passes, which is exactly where Cousins does his work, and 22nd in sack rate, which eases the pressure on a leaky Raiders line. At the same time, the Bills' offense ranks 1st in EPA and 2nd in pass EPA against a Raiders defense that ranks 29th against short throws. A 53.5 total and a six-point spread point to Cousins throwing all game, and this is indoors.

Buffalo's injury list matters if it carries over. DT Ed Oliver, DE Landon Jackson and slot CB Dee Alford were all inactive Monday against the Rams, and Te'Cory Couch has a hamstring issue. Missing interior push and a slot corner help a pocket passer who leans on Bowers and short timing throws. Those reports date from Monday, so check Friday's statuses. On his side, Jalen Nailor (concussion) is expected to practice and would restore a half-time receiver, while Dont'e Thornton remains on IR.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs a leaky underneath defense
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo ranks 27th in EPA allowed on short passes, and Cousins is at his best inside 10 air yards. That favors long, efficient drives and a high completion rate.

keyMatchups.title: Bowers vs Buffalo's tight-end coverage
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo allows 0.42 EPA per target to opposing top tight ends, 23rd in the league, and Alford's absence would thin the middle of the field further. Bowers should be Cousins' first read again.

keyMatchups.title: Bills offense forcing a pass script
keyMatchups.body: With the league's top offense against a Raiders defense that bleeds short completions, Las Vegas will probably trail and have to keep throwing. That raises his attempt ceiling, as in the 52-attempt Chiefs game.

nextGame.watch: Whether Buffalo gets Oliver and Jackson back. If its pass rush stays thin, Cousins has the clean pockets his whole game depends on.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable: a pocket passer with good sack avoidance, a productive short game and Bowers as a high-value target. That should keep him a solid starter by efficiency, likely somewhere in the 0.10-0.17 EPA range rather than near 0.19. Volume will stay healthy because the run game can't carry the offense. The touchdown rate and deep-ball efficiency are the two numbers due to come down, and the intermediate interceptions are a real, long-standing tendency that will keep showing up.

The biggest risk is age and protection. A line ranked 27th in hit rate allowed is a problem for a 38-year-old who doesn't move. If the pressure rate climbs above its current 22%, the bad-throw and turnover numbers tend to follow, as they did in 2025.
swingFactors: Pass protection holding up for a stationary 38-year-old
Whether the run game improves enough to cut his volume

bets.reason: Buffalo allows 314 passing yards a game (31st) and ranks 27th against short passes, his best area. A 53.5 total and a six-point deficit point to heavy volume indoors.
He has thrown 2+ touchdowns in four of five games, and Buffalo allows 2.6 passing touchdowns a game (28th). That offsets the expected regression in his red-zone rate.

Las Vegas covered four of five and Buffalo's defense ranks 30th in EPA. Cousins' passing offense ranks 10th and should keep pace at home, though the New England blowout and the Bills' top offense temper this.

The league's top offense faces a Raiders defense ranked 29th against short passes, while Buffalo's 30th-ranked defense meets a top-10 Raiders passing attack, indoors. The number is already high, so the edge is modest.

confidence.note: Five-game sample with small deep and red-zone splits, but a long, consistent career profile.
